investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing Due to Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing in production with identical HTTP 409 conflict errors indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The AURA observability eval cannot provision a new agent to validate VM readiness or runtime state because the upstream swarm layer is rejecting all creation requests.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm backend has reached its hard agent quota limit of 100. Every POST /api/agents request is rejected with a 409 conflict response containing the message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval check depends on successfully creating a new agent to assert vmIdPresent and remoteState, the entire remote-agents feature check tree fails before any evidence can be collected. The quota exhaustion is the singular upstream blocker for all three sibling checks.
proof: HTTP 409 response body on POST /api/agents: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}

All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the identical 409 error message, confirming the failure is not isolated to one check path but is systemic at the swarm creation layer.
evidence:{} on all three checks confirms zero evidence was collected — no agentId, no vmIdPresent, no remoteState — because execution never progressed past the creation step.
Latency for all three failing checks is low (1148–1347 ms), consistent with an immediate rejection at the API gateway or swarm controller rather than a timeout or downstream VM failure.
The expected output contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be asserted when agent creation is blocked at the quota boundary.
The check staleAfterMinutes is 20 and the run was at 2026-06-14T03:41:36Z, meaning this is a fresh failure, not a stale result — the quota was already exhausted at the time of the eval run.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] Swarm agent quota (hard limit: 100) is fully consumed in the production environment by existing live agents, leaving no capacity for new agent provisioning. This is directly stated in the error payload.
[Medium confidence] AURA eval agents created by previous check runs were not cleaned up after each run, causing quota slots to accumulate over time until the limit was reached.
[Medium confidence] A separate workload or tenant in the same swarm namespace consumed quota slots independently of the AURA eval runner, exhausting capacity without the eval system's awareness.
[Lower confidence] The quota limit of 100 is misconfigured or too low for the current production scale, and legitimate user-created agents alone are sufficient to exhaust it under normal load.
[Lower confidence] A swarm controller bug is failing to release quota slots when agents are deleted or terminated, causing phantom quota consumption that does not reflect actual running agents.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously in production at 2026-06-14T03:41Z with identical HTTP 409 conflict errors indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. Because agent creation is a prerequisite for state polling and runtime readiness, no check in the remote-agents feature could produce the required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state).
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with a 409 conflict error whose inner message explicitly states "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The observability eval environment shares (or is subject to) the same per-org or global swarm agent quota as production workloads. The quota is exhausted, so no new agent can be provisioned, causing every downstream check that depends on a freshly created agent to fail with no evidence collected.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three checks: remote-agent-create (latency 1347ms, endedAt 03:41:28.334Z), remote-agent-state (latency 1148ms, endedAt 03:41:29.482Z), and remote-agent-runtime (latency 1239ms, endedAt 03:41:30.721Z).
Inner swarm error message is unambiguous: 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the quota ceiling has been reached.

All three checks carry identical error payloads ({"error":"swarm agent already exists", "code":"conflict", "details":null}), ruling out a transient or isolated failure and pointing to a shared quota constraint.
evidence:{} on every check confirms zero required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were collected, consistent with creation failing before any state could be observed.
Failure window spans at least 2.387 seconds (03:41:28.334Z – 03:41:30.721Z) across sequential checks, indicating the quota was already exhausted at the start of the eval run, not hit mid-run.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The swarm agent quota (limit=100) is exhausted in the target org or environment because previously provisioned eval agents were not cleaned up after prior runs, accumulating until the ceiling was hit.
[Likely] A prior eval run or automated process created agents but crashed or was interrupted before executing teardown/delete logic, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
[Possible] The observability eval uses the same org/quota namespace as production or staging workloads, and organic user growth in agent count has consumed the remaining quota headroom.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 is a hard system-wide ceiling that has not been raised to accommodate the current scale of production usage plus eval overhead.

[Less likely] A duplicate-creation guard in the swarm backend is misidentifying the eval agent as an already-existing agent ('swarm agent already exists') due to a naming/ID collision, triggering the quota error as a secondary effect.

investigation.rootCause: The production swarm has reached its hard agent quota limit of 100. Every attempt to POST /api/agents returns a 409 conflict with the message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", preventing the AURA observability eval from provisioning a test agent. This is most likely caused by leaked or un-reaped eval agents from prior runs accumulating against the quota, or by legitimate production agents consuming the full allocation, leaving no headroom for ephemeral eval agents.
proof: remote-agent-runtime check: POST /api/agents → HTTP 409, error: "swarm agent already exists: conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100"

The nested error payload contains both an outer AURA-layer message and an inner swarm-layer structured error {code: conflict, message: conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100}, confirming the quota enforcement originates in the swarm backend, not the AURA API layer

[High confidence] A prior eval run crashed or was interrupted before its cleanup/teardown phase, leaving one or more orphaned agents registered in the swarm.
[Medium confidence] Legitimate production remote agents have grown to consume the full quota of 100, leaving zero capacity for ephemeral eval agents — the eval has no reserved quota slot.
[Low confidence] A race condition between concurrent eval runs caused multiple agents to be created simultaneously, each believing quota was available, collectively exhausting the limit.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigation.summary: The image generation stream check failed immediately after `generation_start` because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame before any progress or completion frames could be produced. Both required evidence fields (`frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent`) are absent, confirming the stream never advanced past session initialization.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The HTTP 404 response during session open indicates either the harness process is not running, the deployment is missing or misconfigured, or the harness version deployed does not expose the expected session endpoint path — preventing any image generation work from starting.
proof: Frame 2 (generation_error) carries code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED with message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
The stream contains only 3 frames: generation_start, generation_error, and an empty message frame — no progress frames, no generation_completed frame, and no artifact URL were ever emitted.
Required evidence fields 'frameTypes' and 'imageUrlPresent' are both missing from the eval evidence object, confirming zero successful stream output.
Check latency was 2028 ms (well under the 180 000 ms warning threshold), consistent with an immediate connection failure rather than a timeout or slow generation.

The check ran in the 'production' environment at 2026-06-14T03:41:30Z and is marked required with a 30-minute staleness window, meaning this failure directly blocks the feature's production health signal.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The agent runtime harness process is not running or was never deployed to the target host, causing every request to the session-open endpoint to return 404.
[Likely] LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL is misconfigured (wrong host, port, or base path), pointing the eval harness at a server that does not host the agent runtime.
[Likely] A recent harness deployment changed the session endpoint path or API version, making the previously valid URL return 404 (version incompatibility as stated in the error message).
[Possible] A network or infrastructure change (DNS update, load-balancer rule, ingress reconfiguration) broke routing to the harness endpoint after the last successful check.
[Less likely] The harness is running but behind an auth layer or firewall that returns 404 instead of 401/403 for unauthenticated requests from the eval runner.

followUpEvals: harness-liveness-probe: A dedicated eval that performs a lightweight HTTP GET to the harness health or ping endpoint and asserts a 200 response, running on the same staleness cadence (30 min) as the image generation check.

session-open-latency: An eval that measures time-to-first-frame after session open and alerts if no frame is received within a configurable threshold, catching slow or partially broken harness deployments before they produce full 404s.

harness-version-compatibility: An eval that queries the harness version endpoint and asserts the reported version falls within the range supported by the current eval runner, catching incompatible deployments before stream checks run.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image generation stream check failed immediately after `generation_start` because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame before any progress or completion frames could be produced. Both required evidence fields (`frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent`) are absent, confirming the stream never advanced past session initialization.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The HTTP 404 response during session open indicates either the harness process is not running, the deployment is missing or misconfigured, or the harness version deployed does not expose the expected session endpoint path — preventing any image generation work from starting.
proof: Frame 2 (generation_error) carries code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED with message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
The stream contains only 3 frames: generation_start, generation_error, and an empty message frame — no progress frames, no generation_completed frame, and no artifact URL were ever emitted.
Required evidence fields 'frameTypes' and 'imageUrlPresent' are both missing from the eval evidence object, confirming zero successful stream output.
Check latency was 2028 ms (well under the 180 000 ms warning threshold), consistent with an immediate connection failure rather than a timeout or slow generation.

The check ran in the 'production' environment at 2026-06-14T03:41:30Z and is marked required with a 30-minute staleness window, meaning this failure directly blocks the feature's production health signal.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The agent runtime harness process is not running or was never deployed to the target host, causing every request to the session-open endpoint to return 404.
[Likely] LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL is misconfigured (wrong host, port, or base path), pointing the eval harness at a server that does not host the agent runtime.
[Likely] A recent harness deployment changed the session endpoint path or API version, making the previously valid URL return 404 (version incompatibility as stated in the error message).
[Possible] A network or infrastructure change (DNS update, load-balancer rule, ingress reconfiguration) broke routing to the harness endpoint after the last successful check.
[Less likely] The harness is running but behind an auth layer or firewall that returns 404 instead of 401/403 for unauthenticated requests from the eval runner.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing Due to Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing in production with identical HTTP 409 conflict errors indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The AURA observability eval cannot provision a new agent to validate VM readiness or runtime state because the upstream swarm layer is rejecting all creation requests.
investigations.rootCause: The production swarm backend has reached its hard agent quota limit of 100. Every POST /api/agents request is rejected with a 409 conflict response containing the message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval check depends on successfully creating a new agent to assert vmIdPresent and remoteState, the entire remote-agents feature check tree fails before any evidence can be collected. The quota exhaustion is the singular upstream blocker for all three sibling checks.
proof: HTTP 409 response body on POST /api/agents: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}

All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the identical 409 error message, confirming the failure is not isolated to one check path but is systemic at the swarm creation layer.
evidence:{} on all three checks confirms zero evidence was collected — no agentId, no vmIdPresent, no remoteState — because execution never progressed past the creation step.
Latency for all three failing checks is low (1148–1347 ms), consistent with an immediate rejection at the API gateway or swarm controller rather than a timeout or downstream VM failure.
The expected output contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be asserted when agent creation is blocked at the quota boundary.
The check staleAfterMinutes is 20 and the run was at 2026-06-14T03:41:36Z, meaning this is a fresh failure, not a stale result — the quota was already exhausted at the time of the eval run.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] Swarm agent quota (hard limit: 100) is fully consumed in the production environment by existing live agents, leaving no capacity for new agent provisioning. This is directly stated in the error payload.
[Medium confidence] AURA eval agents created by previous check runs were not cleaned up after each run, causing quota slots to accumulate over time until the limit was reached.
[Medium confidence] A separate workload or tenant in the same swarm namespace consumed quota slots independently of the AURA eval runner, exhausting capacity without the eval system's awareness.
[Lower confidence] The quota limit of 100 is misconfigured or too low for the current production scale, and legitimate user-created agents alone are sufficient to exhaust it under normal load.
[Lower confidence] A swarm controller bug is failing to release quota slots when agents are deleted or terminated, causing phantom quota consumption that does not reflect actual running agents.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously in production at 2026-06-14T03:41Z with identical HTTP 409 conflict errors indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The observability eval environment shares (or is subject to) the same per-org or global swarm agent quota as production workloads. The quota is exhausted, so no new agent can be provisioned, causing every downstream check that depends on a freshly created agent to fail with no evidence collected.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three checks: remote-agent-create (latency 1347ms, endedAt 03:41:28.334Z), remote-agent-state (latency 1148ms, endedAt 03:41:29.482Z), and remote-agent-runtime (latency 1239ms, endedAt 03:41:30.721Z).
Inner swarm error message is unambiguous: 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the quota ceiling has been reached.

All three checks carry identical error payloads ({"error":"swarm agent already exists", "code":"conflict", "details":null}), ruling out a transient or isolated failure and pointing to a shared quota constraint.
evidence:{} on every check confirms zero required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were collected, consistent with creation failing before any state could be observed.
Failure window spans at least 2.387 seconds (03:41:28.334Z – 03:41:30.721Z) across sequential checks, indicating the quota was already exhausted at the start of the eval run, not hit mid-run.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The swarm agent quota (limit=100) is exhausted in the target org or environment because previously provisioned eval agents were not cleaned up after prior runs, accumulating until the ceiling was hit.
[Likely] A prior eval run or automated process created agents but crashed or was interrupted before executing teardown/delete logic, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
[Possible] The observability eval uses the same org/quota namespace as production or staging workloads, and organic user growth in agent count has consumed the remaining quota headroom.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 is a hard system-wide ceiling that has not been raised to accommodate the current scale of production usage plus eval overhead.

[Less likely] A duplicate-creation guard in the swarm backend is misidentifying the eval agent as an already-existing agent ('swarm agent already exists') due to a naming/ID collision, triggering the quota error as a secondary effect.
